correctness.rationale: The proof is symbolic. For X=Gr(k,n), T_X=S^* tensor Q gives c1(T_X)=nH, hence K_X=-nH. Adjunction on a general (d-1)-fold Pluecker hyperplane section, d=k(n-k), gives 2g-2=(d-1-n)D. Sturmfels Theorem 1.1 then gives Hdeg=2D+2g-2=(d+1-n)D=(k-1)(n-k-1)D. Kohn Theorem 9 identifies the Hurwitz degree with delta_1 and delta_0 with D. The checker verifies the hook-length degree, integrality of the genus, duality, and the resulting identity on a large finite grid.

value.rationale: The Hurwitz form is the discriminant governing non-reduced complementary linear sections, and its degree enters complexity and conditioning estimates for numerical intersection. Ordinary Grassmannians are a central test family in projective geometry. The result turns the abstract sectional-genus formula into an explicit uniform multiplicative law, simultaneously determining the first polar degree from the Chow degree and isolating the Klein quadric as the unique equal-degree case. This is a structural family-wide invariant rather than an isolated numerical computation.
